The '''Rane Group''' is an Indian industrial conglomerate, headquartered in [[Chennai]]. Beginning as a dealer for automobile, trucks and auto-parts in Madras in the 1920s, Rane has grown to encompass ten different companies as of 2013.

== Scope ==

According to the company's web site, its sales for fiscal 2012–13 were {{INRConvert|52.36|b|lk=r}}.<ref name="Off site about group">{{cite web|url=http://ranegroup.com/about/|title=Rane Group|work=Rane Group Official site|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref>

According to ''The Automotive Horizon'' the company has "dominat[ed] the domestic [Indian] auto component space" for "decades".<ref name="AutoHorizMenon-Outside" />

In 2020 the group had manufacturing facilities in [[Chennai]], [[Puducherry (city)|Puducherry]], [[Hyderabad]], [[Mysore]], [[Tumkur]], [[Pantnagar]], [[Bawal]], [[Tiruchirappalli|Trichy]], [[Sanand]].<ref name="BuisStd-20Jun11">{{cite news|title=Rane group to invest Rs 239 cr|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/rane-group-to-invest-rs-239-cr-111062000060_1.html|work=Business Standard|date=20 June 2011|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref> and [[Russellville, Kentucky]]

== Activities ==

In late 2011 the group entered the defense and aerospace market by purchasing a 26% equity stake in SasMos HET Technologies Pvt Ltd. SasMos manufactures interconnection systems (cable harnesses) for various defence and aerospace purposes. Group chairman L. Ganesh was quoted as saying that he foresaw "significant growth opportunities both in India and as an exporter."

The Rane Group was, as of 2012, planning to establish a manufacturing plant outside India.<ref name="AutoHorizMenon-Outside">{{cite web|url=http://automotivehorizon.sulekha.com/rane-group-to-establish-manufacturing-plant-outside_newsitem_5602|title=Rane Group to establish manufacturing plant outside India| first=Jayashankar|last=Menon|work=The Automotive Horizon|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref> Group chairman L. Ganesh was quoted as saying: "We think the time has come to look beyond India, to see if there is more space to grow, and, if it makes sense to manufacture there as well. While our Tier-I products will still continue to be made with our joint venture partners, we are studying global markets to see if it’s feasible to manufacture our Tier-II products such as engine valves there."<ref name="AutoHorizMenon-Outside"/><ref name="Hindu-25Oct12">{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/rane-group-looking-at-production-base-abroad/article4031716.ece|title=Rane Group looking at production base abroad|work=The Hindu|date=25 October 2012|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref>
In 2011 the group planned to reinvest around {{INR}}2,392 million, an increase from {{INR}}2,173 million the previous year.<ref name="BuisStd-20Jun11"/> However, in September 2013 the group was reported to have scaled back from a planned investment of about {{INR}}2.50 billion to {{INR}}1.30 billion in both the previous and coming fiscal years, because of economic slowdowns.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rane Group to hold back 50% of Rs 500 crore investments|url=http://zeenews.india.com/business/automobiles/auto-news/rane-group-to-hold-back-50-of-rs-500-crore-investments_83363.html|work=Zee News India|date=5 September 2013|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref>

== Reactions ==

[[Moneycontrol.com]] ran a video story about "succession planning" in the Rane Group, and how "dynastic rules" are accepted in Indian business while they are opposed in politics.<ref name="MC-Making It Big">{{cite news|url=http://www.moneycontrol.com/news/special-videos/making-it-big-the-storyrane-group_679257.html|title=Making it big: The story of Rane Group!|date=13 March 2012|work=moneycontrol.com|publisher=e-Eighteen.com Ltd.|accessdate=5 January 2014}}</ref>
